written.myAnswer: An element’s chemical formula represents one kind of atom, for example Na or O₂. A compound’s formula represents two or more kinds of atoms in a fixed ratio, for example H₂O or NaCl.

Ionic compounds: sodium chloride (NaCl), calcium chloride (CaCl₂), potassium bromide (KBr) and barium chloride (BaCl₂). Covalent compounds: hydrogen chloride (HCl), hydrogen fluoride (HF), hydrogen sulfide (H₂S), phosphine (PH₃), hydrogen peroxide (H₂O₂), sulfuric acid (H₂SO₄), carbon dioxide (CO₂), carbon monoxide (CO), benzene (C₆H₆), water (H₂O), ammonia (NH₃) and methane (CH₄).
Calcium phosphate: Ca₃(PO₄)₂; aluminium nitride: AlN; sodium acetate: CH₃COONa; ammonium carbonate: (NH₄)₂CO₃; bismuth sulphate: Bi₂(SO₄)₃.

The statement is not entirely correct: different compounds can have the same molecular formula, as structural isomers do. Different compounds can also share an empirical formula; for example, ethene (C₂H₄) and propene (C₃H₆) both have the empirical formula CH₂.
Sand is a giant network solid rather than a collection of discrete SiO₂ molecules. Its formula, SiO₂, gives the simplest ratio of silicon atoms to oxygen atoms in the structure: 1:2.
